prs.author: Dharit13

(2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3041 splits the whole header into top-level comma segments and then explicitly matches the segment whose scheme token is 'bearer' via partition(' '), so it correctly scopes extraction to the Bearer challenge when a header contains multiple auth-schemes/challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"'). #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only strips text up to the header's first space and then treats everything after it as one flat list of comma-separated params, so it never re-establishes a scheme boundary and would still mis-parse a header containing more than one challenge/scheme -- the same class of boundary bug both PRs set out to fix.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string parameter value whose annotation isn't the bare `str` type, so a plain string that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON blob passed as a `str | None` field) gets silently corrupted into a dict/list before Pydantic validation. Both PRs patch the exact same `pre_parse_json` skip-condition to stop that for str-containing unions. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string parameter value whose annotation isn't the bare `str` type, so a plain string that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON blob passed as a `str | None` field) gets silently corrupted into a dict/list before Pydantic validation. Both PRs patch the exact same `pre_parse_json` skip-condition to stop that for str-containing unions. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip JSON decoding for str-unions, but #3056's `_is_optional_str` first calls `_unwrap_annotated` on each union member, so it correctly recognizes the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter shape used throughout this codebase for describing string args. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead checks raw membership in a frozenset of bare types (`str, int, float, bool, NoneType`); since `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not equal to `str` under that check, a union like `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is still classified as needing pre-parsing, leaving the original corruption bug in place for that common case. #2032 does additionally cover other all-simple-type unions (e.g. `str | int`), which #3056 doesn't touch, but those cases aren't lossy in the same way (a numeric-looking string decoded to an int is still a valid member of a str|int union), whereas the str|None corruption is the actual reported failure mode.

prs.title: fix(client/auth): discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh, with issuer-binding check
prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, `OAuthContext.oauth_metadata` exists only in memory and is lost, so a cold-start token refresh can't resolve the authorization server's token endpoint without rediscovering metadata. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, `OAuthContext.oauth_metadata` exists only in memory and is lost, so a cold-start token refresh can't resolve the authorization server's token endpoint without rediscovering metadata. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Resolves the missing-metadata case without requiring any change to the `TokenStorage` protocol or to existing storage backends: it runs AS metadata discovery before the cold-start refresh, uses the new `eager_discovery_attempted` flag to avoid re-probing on every in-process refresh, and adds an issuer-binding check on the discovered metadata that #2492 does not include. #2492's fix relies on storage implementations actually persisting `oauth_metadata` via new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods it adds to `TokenStorage`, but those methods default to no-ops (`return None`), so any storage backend not explicitly updated to implement persistence is left with the original bug after restart.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip JSON decoding for str-unions, but #3056's `_is_optional_str` first calls `_unwrap_annotated` on each union member, so it correctly recognizes the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter shape used throughout this codebase for describing string args. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead checks raw membership in a frozenset of bare types (`str, int, float, bool, NoneType`); since `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not equal to `str` under that check, a union like `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is still classified as needing pre-parsing, leaving the original corruption bug in place for that common case. #2032 does additionally cover other all-simple-type unions (e.g. `str | int`), which #3056 doesn't touch, but those cases aren't lossy in the same way (a numeric-looking string decoded to an int is still a valid member of a str|int union), whereas the str|None corruption is the actual reported failure mode.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs target the same silent-return branch in _handle_reconnection. #2395 fixes it in place: it checks isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest) and sends a JSONRPCError carrying the original request's id to ctx.read_stream_writer, so only that specific outstanding request resolves with an error while other in-flight requests on the session are untouched; it also removes the pre-existing `# pragma: no cover` on that branch, indicating the new path is exercised by a test. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError from the reconnection path and adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull it back out of the resulting anyio ExceptionGroup after the fact; since the exception propagates up through the TaskGroup, it would tear down the whole transport/session rather than resolving just the one affected request, and its diff also carries an unrelated change (dropping the `_annotations` import alias) that isn't needed for the fix.

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 splits the whole header into top-level comma segments and then explicitly matches the segment whose scheme token is 'bearer' via partition(' '), so it correctly scopes extraction to the Bearer challenge when a header contains multiple auth-schemes/challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"'). #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only strips text up to the header's first space and then treats everything after it as one flat list of comma-separated params, so it never re-establishes a scheme boundary and would still mis-parse a header containing more than one challenge/scheme -- the same class of boundary bug both PRs set out to fix.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip JSON decoding for str-unions, but #3056's `_is_optional_str` first calls `_unwrap_annotated` on each union member, so it correctly recognizes the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter shape used throughout this codebase for describing string args. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead checks raw membership in a frozenset of bare types (`str, int, float, bool, NoneType`); since `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not equal to `str` under that check, a union like `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is still classified as needing pre-parsing, leaving the original corruption bug in place for that common case. #2032 does additionally cover other all-simple-type unions (e.g. `str | int`), which #3056 doesn't touch, but those cases aren't lossy in the same way (a numeric-looking string decoded to an int is still a valid member of a str|int union), whereas the str|None corruption is the actual reported failure mode.

clusters.pick_reason: #2654 changes the default write_stream buffer from 0 to 1, so the blocking-on-progress-notification bug is fixed for all callers without requiring opt-in, whereas #2215 leaves both defaults at 0 and only fixes the issue if a caller discovers and passes a non-default buffer size. #2654 also adds a dedicated regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces a slow/blocking stdout write and asserts a queued response isn't stalled behind it, directly exercising the failure mode; #2215's diff only shows the signature/stream-creation change with no equivalent scenario test included. #2654's diff is also narrower (single line change to the write stream buffer plus comment) versus #2215's broader public API change (two new constructor parameters on stdio_server), which is more surface area to review and maintain for a fix that doesn't change default behavior.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs target the same silent-return branch in _handle_reconnection. #2395 fixes it in place: it checks isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest) and sends a JSONRPCError carrying the original request's id to ctx.read_stream_writer, so only that specific outstanding request resolves with an error while other in-flight requests on the session are untouched; it also removes the pre-existing `# pragma: no cover` on that branch, indicating the new path is exercised by a test. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError from the reconnection path and adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull it back out of the resulting anyio ExceptionGroup after the fact; since the exception propagates up through the TaskGroup, it would tear down the whole transport/session rather than resolving just the one affected request, and its diff also carries an unrelated change (dropping the `_annotations` import alias) that isn't needed for the fix.

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 splits the whole header into top-level comma segments and then explicitly matches the segment whose scheme token is 'bearer' via partition(' '), so it correctly scopes extraction to the Bearer challenge when a header contains multiple auth-schemes/challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"'). #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only strips text up to the header's first space and then treats everything after it as one flat list of comma-separated params, so it never re-establishes a scheme boundary and would still mis-parse a header containing more than one challenge/scheme -- the same class of boundary bug both PRs set out to fix.
